title: Sample matching for extinction gradients (review branch)
abstract:
**Review branch, not a merge request.** This exists so the changes and the
evidence behind them can be read in one place before anything is proposed
upstream.

## Description

Sample matching for extinction gradients in volumetric inverse rendering, as
a new integrator plugin, plus the medium-side machinery it needs.

> Ruihan Yu, Yu-Chen Wang, Jingwang Ling, Feng Xu, Shuang Zhao.
> **Sample Matching for Joint Extinction Gradient Estimation in Differentiable
> Volume Rendering.** ACM Transactions on Graphics 45(4), 2026.
> [paper](https://auroraryan0301.github.io/samplematching/static/papers/sample_matching_paper.pdf)
> · [supplementary](https://auroraryan0301.github.io/samplematching/static/papers/sample_matching_supplementary.pdf)
> · [project page](https://auroraryan0301.github.io/samplematching/)
> · [doi:10.1145/3811329](https://doi.org/10.1145/3811329)

Differentiating volumetric transport with respect to the extinction
coefficient produces two contributions of opposite sign: a **scattering**
term, because denser media scatter more light toward the camera, and a
**transmittance** term, because denser media attenuate everything passing
through. Existing estimators evaluate the two at unrelated points, so their
negative correlation does nothing for you. This integrator evaluates both at
shared locations along each path segment, which turns that correlation
into a variance reduction.

### New plugin

`prbvolpath_sm` — sample-matching volumetric PRB. Primal rendering is
identical to `prbvolpath`; all of the new machinery runs in the adjoint pass.

`segment_slots` selects between two estimators:

| value | behaviour | also registered as |
|---|---|---|
| `max_depth + 1` (default) | every completed segment gets a record slot and is sampled | `prbvolpath_sm_quad` |
| `1` | one weighted reservoir per lane; the retained segment stands in for the whole path, scaled by the inverse selection probability | `prbvolpath_sm_linear` |

Segment *j* of a lane goes to slot `min(j, segment_slots - 1)`. The first
`segment_slots - 1` are always kept; everything from there on shares one
reserved row per lane and is resolved by a weighted reservoir. Both halves
are unbiased on their own, so the estimator is unbiased at every slot count —
the count only moves the split between segments sampled exactly and segments
pooled into one. Nothing is ever dropped.

**Two megakernels, not one.** In the adjoint pass the path tracing and the
`dr.backward` that follows it run as two separate megakernels. The reason is
OptiX: the gradient sampling on a segment traces rays of its own, and every
trace inside a loop saves and restores whatever is still alive across the
iteration. Keeping a segment's record in loop state — named variables or
`dr.alloc_local`, measured identical — cost +2.5 KiB/thread of continuation
spills and +45% adjoint time on the bunny, and nothing at all under analytic
intersection. So the path loop does no gradient sampling. It writes one small
record per segment with a masked scatter, the values die at the end of the
iteration, and the second kernel reads them back and does the sampling there,
one lane per record. Only one scalar stays in loop state: the reservoir's
running weight.

**Spectral and RGB.** Both are supported, including an extinction that varies
across channels. Deferred record fields are generated from the variant's
spectrum size, and each record carries the path's wavelengths so the second
kernel evaluates the medium at the right ones.

**What was tried and dropped: reconnection (paper Sec. 5.1, Eq. 32-34).** The
the gradient samples on a segment can reuse the path's own continuation
instead of tracing a fresh sub-path each, which is much cheaper. It was implemented and
verified unbiased by finite differences. It is not in this branch: at equal
iteration count its variance is *worse* than tracing the sub-paths. The shift
mapping connects two points with different visibility, so the reuse weight
carries a transmittance ratio that ranged over `1e-9` to `356` in
measurements, and only 4.8% of the samples could reuse at all. The archived branch
keeps the measurements.

### Changes to existing code

- **`Medium`**: a majorant supergrid, on by default
  (`majorant_resolution_factor` 8, `majorant_factor` 1.2), traversed with a
  DDA. Empty and thin regions are crossed in far fewer null collisions
  instead of paying for the densest voxel in the volume. `homogeneous`
  rejects the parameter explicitly, since it cannot honour it.
- **`Medium::sample_real_interaction`**: consumes null collisions in one
  fused C++ walk instead of iterating them in Python. With a supergrid the
  DDA traversal and the null-collision walk share a single loop.
- **`heterogeneous` takes either parameterization.** The scattering
  coefficient can be given as an `albedo` volume or as `sigma_s` directly;
  the two are mutually exclusive and the plugin says so. This follows the DRT
  implementation, which pairs albedo with `sigma_t` to decouple the two and
  keep optimization gradients stable — with `sigma_s` given independently the
  derivative involves `sigma_s / sigma_t` and goes unstable as the extinction
  goes to zero.

  The integrators always *query* `sigma_s`; what is differentiable is a
  separate matter, handled the way the rest of Mitsuba handles it. `traverse`
  exposes whichever of the two the scene gave — never both — alongside
  `sigma_t`, each marked `ParamFlags::Differentiable`, and `scale` marked
  `NonDifferentiable`. That declares what may carry a gradient; nothing does
  until the caller enables one, exactly as `Mesh` declares `vertex_positions`
  differentiable and `faces` not. So the query surface is fixed and the
  parameterization you optimize is a scene-authoring choice.
- **`Medium::get_albedo`**: a direct albedo lookup, no production caller in
  this branch. It is a cheaper and better-conditioned query than rebuilding
  `sigma_s / sigma_t`, which is `0/0` wherever the extinction vanishes.

`prbvolpath.py` is untouched.

## Testing

Numbers below are on an A40 under CUDA/OptiX unless stated. The variant
matrix is at the end of this section.

### Single-channel extinction

This is the case the method is about; the three-channel one below is a
capability this branch adds.

#### Gradient mean and variance against DRT

Per-voxel statistics at equal iteration count, against the differential delta
tracking implementation this work builds on (`volpathsimple`, max depth 64,
subsampling off — its quadratic setting, so it is compared against a slot per
segment like for like).
Bunny cloud, 768x576, uniform white environment, 8 spp, N = 512 adjoint
renders with identical seeds, `gradient_samples_per_segment` 4, at a checkpoint from a
real training run. Central slice along each axis.

![gradient mean](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AuroraRyan0301/mitsuba3/pr-figures/fig_grad_mean.png)

Every row integrates to the same value, and to the forward finite-difference
truth for this scene, -1.1829e+08:

| estimator | integrated gradient |
|---|---|
| DRT reference, max depth 64 (quadratic) | -1.1830e+08 |
| sample matching, one record slot per lane (linear) | -1.1828e+08 |
| sample matching, four record slots (linear, large constant) | -1.1829e+08 |
| sample matching, a slot per segment (quadratic) | -1.1828e+08 |

![gradient variance](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AuroraRyan0301/mitsuba3/pr-figures/fig_grad_var.png)

| estimator | variance, occupied voxels | variance, all voxels | vs DRT |
|---|---|---|---|
| DRT reference, max depth 64 (quadratic) | 136.5 | 318.9 | 1.00x |
| sample matching, one record slot per lane (linear) | 61.8 | 91.5 | 0.29x |
| sample matching, four record slots (linear, large constant) | 46.4 | 81.4 | 0.26x |
| sample matching, a slot per segment (quadratic) | 45.4 | 80.9 | 0.25x |

Variance drops to a quarter, and most of that is empty space: over occupied
voxels the reference is at 136.5 against 45.4, but counting empty ones it is
at 318.9 against 80.9. The first row of the variance figure shows it — the
reference is hot everywhere around the bunny, the sample-matching rows are
not. Four slots already capture nearly all of the gain; going from four to a
slot per segment moves the variance by 1%.

#### Inverse rendering

Bunny cloud, 63 training views, pixel batching (batch 32768), 1024/16 spp,
Adam at 6e-3, coarse-to-fine 64^3 -> 128^3 -> 256^3, Russian roulette off, L1
loss, 8000 iterations. PSNR on a held-out view, measured by re-rendering the
optimized volume with `prbvolpath` so the metric does not depend on the
estimator that produced it.

| integrator | complexity in path length | `gradient_samples_per_segment` | PSNR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `prbvolpath` | linear | — | 24.84 dB |
| `prbvolpath_sm_quad` | quadratic | 4 | **38.58 dB** |
| `prbvolpath_sm_linear` | linear | 4 | 35.87 dB |

`prbvolpath` plateaus rather than converging slowly: 24.03 dB at iteration
4000, 24.77 dB at 8000.

### Three-channel extinction

The extinction varies across channels here. All channels share one majorant
and one accept/reject coin, so this is the path the correction described
above applies to; a gray grid makes that correction identically 1.

#### Gradients against finite differences

Central differences, directional derivative along a fixed perturbation:

| integrator | `gradient_samples_per_segment` | RGB, rel. error | spectral, rel. error |
|---|---|---|---|
| `prbvolpath` | — | 0.0121 | 0.0350 |
| `prbvolpath_sm_quad` | 1 (default) | 0.0124 | 0.0166 |
| `prbvolpath_sm_quad` | 4 | 0.0125 | 0.0180 |
| `prbvolpath_sm_linear` | 1 (default) | 0.0118 | 0.0174 |

#### Inverse rendering

Same configuration as above, with a three-channel extinction grid:

| integrator | complexity | `gradient_samples_per_segment` | 4000 iterations | 8000 iterations |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `prbvolpath` | linear | — | 24.84 dB | 23.45 dB |
| `prbvolpath_sm_quad` | quadratic | 4 | **34.86 dB** | **35.02 dB** |
| `prbvolpath_sm_linear` | linear | 4 | 31.70 dB | 31.97 dB |

Lower than the single-channel numbers because the reference volume is gray:
three channels give the optimizer two redundant degrees of freedom.

### Stress groups, cost and unit tests

#### Stress groups

46 PASS, 1 WARN. `gones` — the projection `<g,1>` over a grid with carved
zero-density voxels, against forward finite differences — gives 0.999 for
both configurations. `gradfull` is 30/30 across boundary x emitter x
{sigma, albedo}. `media` is 13/13. The single WARN is `prbvolpath` itself at
ratio 2.265 in that projection; its detached estimator is biased in
zero-density regions, which is why it is a documented control there and not a
reference.

#### Cost

One full training step, all implementations timed in the same process, on an
A40 through OptiX. The medium boundary is a real mesh with a null BSDF, so
every ray goes through `optixTrace`; there is no analytic bounding-box
shortcut anywhere in this measurement.

A step is two launches, one wavefront each, no splitting:

| launch | lanes |
|---|---|
| primal | 32768 pixels x 1024 spp = 33 554 432 |
| adjoint | 32768 pixels x 16 spp = 524 288 |

GPU utilization is sampled with `nvidia-smi` at 5 Hz over each timing window:

| integrator | `gradient_samples_per_segment` | s / iteration | vs `prbvolpath` | SM utilization |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `prbvolpath` | — | 1.239 | 1.00x | 99.0% |
| `prbvolpath_sm_quad` | 1 (default) | 0.501 | 0.40x | 93.0% |
| `prbvolpath_sm_quad` | 4 | 0.676 | 0.55x | 93.6% |
| `prbvolpath_sm_linear` | 1 (default) | 0.490 | 0.40x | 92.8% |
| `prbvolpath_sm_linear` | 4 | 0.659 | 0.53x | 92.1% |

Every row keeps the GPU busy, so the gap is not an occupancy effect: sample
matching runs at slightly *lower* utilization than `prbvolpath` and is still
2.5x faster per step.

Raising `gradient_samples_per_segment` from 1 to 4 costs about 35%. The
variance figures above are at 4; at 1 the plugin is still well under
`prbvolpath`.

Memory is where the two slot counts part company. Each configuration was
measured in its own process, against an idle window taken after the scene and
the references are loaded but before any integrator has run:

| integrator | device memory | above idle |
|---|---|---|
| `prbvolpath` | 3693 MiB | 2434 MiB |
| `prbvolpath_sm_quad` | 8301 MiB | 7042 MiB |
| `prbvolpath_sm_linear` | 3725 MiB | 2466 MiB |

The append region is sized by slot count times wavefront, so a slot per
segment costs about 4.6 GB more than `prbvolpath` at this wavefront, while
one slot per lane costs 32 MiB more. `gradient_samples_per_segment` does not
enter into it -- 1 and 4 give the same figure.

Sample matching is faster per step here because it consumes null collisions
inside one fused C++ walk, where `prbvolpath` spends one symbolic-loop
iteration on each of them and pays an `optixTrace` for every one. That is
visible without any of the gradient machinery: rendering the same frame at 64
spp with no AD graph at all, `prbvolpath` takes 104.5 s and this plugin
72.1 s, running the identical estimator in primal mode.

The same measurement shows the gradient sampling never runs in the primal
pass: 72.09 s at `gradient_samples_per_segment` 1 against 72.16 s at 4.

On a smaller microbenchmark that stresses the gradient sampling instead, it
is 1.2-1.55x slower in RGB and 0.74-0.82x in spectral variants.

#### Unit tests

330 pass (`src/media/tests`, `src/integrators/tests`). What each one holds:

| test | checks | RGB | spectral |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test01_primal_matches_prbvolpath` | primal output matches `prbvolpath` | yes | — |
| `test02_gradients_match_prbvolpath` | extinction gradients match `prbvolpath`, all three configurations | yes | — |
| `test03_medium_get_albedo` | `get_albedo` agrees with `sigma_s / sigma_t` for both built-in media | yes | — |
| `test04_primal_matches_prbvolpath_spectral` | primal, three-channel extinction | — | yes |
| `test05_gradients_match_prbvolpath_spectral` | gradients, three-channel extinction | — | yes |
| `test06_gradients_colored_extinction` | gradients when `sigma_t` varies across channels | yes | — |
| `test01_primal_parity` (supergrid) | supergrid renders match the global majorant, several safety factors | yes | — |
| `test02_gradient_parity` (supergrid) | supergrid gradients match the global majorant | yes | — |
| `test03_homogeneous_rejects_supergrid` | `homogeneous` refuses the parameter it cannot honour | yes | — |
| `test04_bounds_extinction_rgb` | the supergrid bound holds above `sigma_t` everywhere | yes | — |
| `test05_bounds_extinction_spectral` | same, where three channels are stored as sRGB model coefficients | — | yes |

Each gradient test runs all three configurations: a slot per segment, a slot
per segment with four gradient samples, and the one-slot reservoir.

#### Variants

The same selection, `src/media/tests` and `src/integrators/tests`, was run on
both backends. Identical result on each:

| backend | variants exercised | tests |
|---|---|---|
| CUDA/OptiX | `cuda_ad_rgb`, `cuda_ad_spectral` | 330 pass |
| LLVM | `llvm_ad_rgb`, `llvm_ad_spectral` | 330 pass |
| scalar | `scalar_rgb`, `scalar_spectral` | builds; the integrator needs a vectorized AD variant, so nothing to run |

The `gones` stress group was also re-run on `llvm_ad_rgb`, since it is the
projection that catches gradients lost in empty voxels. It reproduces the
CUDA result, including the documented `prbvolpath` control:

| cell | LLVM | CUDA |
|---|---|---|
| a slot per segment | 1.001 PASS | 0.999 PASS |
| one slot per lane | 1.001 PASS | 0.999 PASS |
| `prbvolpath` control | 2.268 WARN | 2.265 WARN |
